title: De Novo Mutations in the Sodium-Channel Gene SCN1A Cause Severe

acmg_tags.justification: Null nonsense variant (p.Arg1245Ter) in SCN1A where loss of function is a well-established mechanism of Dravet syndrome.
De novo variant in Patient SMEI-1 with both parents testing negative and paternity genetically confirmed.

assertions.verbatim_quote: In Patient SMEI-1, we identified a de novo heterozygous nonsense mutation c.3733C>T (p.Arg1245Ter) in exon 19.

grounded_phenotypes.label: Febrile seizure (within the age range of 3 months to 6 years)

variant.functional_domain: S4 transmembrane voltage-sensor segment of domain II

assertions.functional_assay_result: Whole-cell patch-clamp recordings in HEK293 cells expressing mutant SCN1A p.Arg739Gln demonstrated complete loss of functional sodium current density compared to wild-type NaV1.1 channels.

acmg_tags.justification: Confirmed de novo heterozygous variant; neither parent carried the c.2216G>A alteration and paternity was confirmed.
Located within the highly conserved S4 transmembrane voltage-sensor segment of domain II.
Whole-cell patch-clamp recordings in HEK293 cells demonstrated complete loss of functional sodium current density.

assertions.verbatim_quote: In Patient SMEI-2, direct sequencing revealed a de novo heterozygous missense substitution c.2216G>A (p.Arg739Gln) located within the highly conserved S4 transmembrane voltage-sensor segment of domain II.

grounded_phenotypes.label: Bilateral tonic-clonic seizure with generalized onset
